problem: Large 3D datasets are mid-sized and cover few categories. ShapeNet has about 51K objects in 55 classes, and embodied-AI simulators such as AI2-THOR/ProcTHOR have only about 2K objects across roughly 100 types. As a result, 3D generative models, long-tail 2D perception and ObjectNav (limited to about 20 target categories) cannot scale to open vocabularies.
motivation: Progress in language and 2D vision came from moving from curated datasets to web-scale data (WebText, LAION, and others), but 3D has no equivalent. Sketchfab hosts hundreds of thousands of Creative-Commons, artist-made and scanned 3D models with names, tags and descriptions. Collecting them could give 3D the scale and diversity needed for generation, perception augmentation and populating simulated homes for embodied agents.
key_idea: Collect 818K CC-licensed, metadata-annotated 3D assets from Sketchfab (Objaverse), build a 47K-object crowd-verified subset mapped to 1,156 LVIS categories (Objaverse-LVIS), and show its value in four applications: GET3D generation, 3D copy-paste segmentation augmentation, open-vocabulary ObjectNav in ProcTHOR houses populated with Objaverse objects, and a rotational-robustness benchmark.
insight: Scale and per-category diversity of 3D assets transfer to downstream tasks. GET3D trained on Objaverse bags was judged more diverse than the ShapeNet-trained model 91% of the time. Pasting renderings of Objaverse-LVIS objects into LVIS images (3DCP) lifts GOL mask AP from 27.7 to 28.3, and rare-category box AP from 19.8 to 21.8. For navigation, the key lesson is that populating procedural houses with tens of thousands of diverse assets lets a plain EmbCLIP-style agent, conditioned on CLIP text embeddings, learn open-vocabulary ObjectNav with good generalization to unseen houses, objects and descriptions. SR rises from 19.9% at 18M steps to 33.0% at about 460M steps. The authors note that the special zero-shot design (target not fed to the RNN) was unnecessary at this data scale. The robustness benchmark shows CLIP models lose about 18–23 Top-1 points between 'any rotation' and 'random rotation', i.e. they overfit to canonical views.
method: Objaverse collection: 818K 3D models from over 100K Sketchfab creators (160K per the Statistics section) via the Sketchfab public API, restricted to distributable Creative Commons licenses and excluding restricted/adult content. Each model keeps its name, 18 coarse categories, free-form tags (>2.35M, >170K unique), description, animations (44K animated objects) and rigs (63K characters). The set also includes 16K+ interior scenes, and coverage is estimated at about 20.8K WordNet entities via CLIP ViT-B/32 thumbnail matching.

Objaverse-LVIS: for each of 1,156 LVIS categories, 500 candidates are selected using CLIP thumbnail similarity plus GloVe similarity of metadata terms. Crowdworkers on MTurk verify about 250K candidates nine at a time, yielding 47K objects each assigned to exactly one category.

3D generative modeling: GET3D is trained on Objaverse subsets (143 shoes, 816 bags, 571 fruits & vegetables across 9 types) and compared against GET3D trained on 83 ShapeNet bags using human diversity judgments.

3DCP (3D copy-paste): 5 views of each Objaverse-LVIS object are rendered and cached. With probability 0.5, 1–3 randomly scaled and translated renders plus their masks are pasted onto an LVIS training image. This augmentation is used to fine-tune the GOL ResNet-50 Mask-RCNN (Gumbel activation) for 24 epochs (batch size 64, lr 0.002).

Open-vocabulary ObjectNav environments: 10,080 ProcTHOR houses (up to 3 rooms) are populated with Objaverse-LVIS assets. Per-category annotations specify placement (floor middle/edge, surface, wall) and a maximum bounding-box size used for scale correction (e.g. bookcase 2 m, fork 0.18 m). Out-of-home categories are filtered out, while doors and windows come from ProcTHOR. Assets are compressed with Blender (merged mesh, ≤5K vertices, a single baked texture), given V-HACD colliders, and loaded at runtime in AI2-THOR.

Open-vocabulary ObjectNav agent: an EmbCLIP architecture with frozen CLIP ResNet-50 visual features on egocentric RGB. The learned target-type embedding is replaced by a linear projection of the CLIP text embedding of 'a {name} {category}', falling back to category only if fastText language detection finds the name is not English. Modality representations are widened from 32-D to 256-D, and an RNN policy is trained with DD-PPO in AllenAct (28 GPUs, 9,421 target assets across 262 categories).

Rotational robustness benchmark: 12 random-orientation renders of each Objaverse-LVIS object on an ImageNet-mean background. Zero-shot CLIP models (restricted to the ~1,200 LVIS classes) are scored on Top-1/Top-5 for a random rotation versus correct from any of the 12 rotations.

setting.backbone: EmbCLIP-style RNN policy trained from scratch with DD-PPO on top of frozen CLIP ResNet-50 visual and text encoders
setting.training_data: 10,080 ProcTHOR procedurally generated houses populated with Objaverse-LVIS assets; 9,421 unique target assets across 262 LVIS categories; main result after 18M simulation steps (extended run of about 460M steps)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (CLIP ResNet-50 features) + CLIP text embedding of the open-vocabulary target description
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookUp, LookDown, End (LoCoBot embodiment; step sizes not stated)
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR (with runtime loading of Objaverse assets)

numbers_note: This is a dataset paper. The open-vocabulary ObjectNav result is only a single SR number (no SPL or other metrics, no tables) on a new self-built benchmark; the random-policy baseline reaches 5.1% SR. The rotational-robustness table (Table 2) evaluates off-the-shelf CLIP models rather than an own method and is omitted; the best Top-1 Random Rotation is 32.9% (LAION-2B ViT-L/14). GET3D results are qualitative plus a human diversity preference of 91% for Objaverse over ShapeNet bags.
results: Objaverse provides 818K 3D objects (vs ShapeNet 51K) covering an estimated ~21K WordNet entities, plus a 47K-object, 1,156-category LVIS-aligned subset. For open-vocabulary ObjectNav across 30 test categories in 151 unseen ProcTHOR houses, the EmbCLIP-style agent reaches 19.9% SR after 18M steps (random policy 5.1%) and 33.0% after about 460M steps. The paper also frames the setup as scaling the objects available in simulation from about 2K to 36K and object types from about 100 to 1.1K. Other results: 3DCP improves the previous LVIS SOTA, GOL, from 27.7 to 28.3 mask AP (21.4 to 21.8 APr), and GET3D trained on Objaverse is judged more diverse than the ShapeNet-trained model 91% of the time.
limitations: The navigation experiment is a proof of concept: a single SR number on the authors' own benchmark, with no SPL, no comparison to other ObjectNav methods, and test categories that are a subset of the training categories (only descriptions, houses and instances are novel).

Assets are uploaded by users and noisy: they need manual scale correction and per-category placement annotation, and doors and windows still come from ProcTHOR. Category frequency does not match the real world (e.g. many swords), and many assets are not English-named.
Objaverse-LVIS covers only up to 500 candidates per category, so many objects remain unlabelled; the segmentation gains are modest (+0.6 mask AP).
